   127→class PassageManager:
   128→    def __init__(
   129→        self, passage_sources: list[dict[str, Any]], metadata_file_path: Optional[str] = None
   130→    ):
   131→        self.offset_maps: dict[str, dict[str, int]] = {}
   132→        self.passage_files: dict[str, str] = {}
   133→        # Avoid materializing a single gigantic global map to reduce memory
   134→        # footprint on very large corpora (e.g., 60M+ passages). Instead, keep
   135→        # per-shard maps and do a lightweight per-shard lookup on demand.
   136→        self._total_count: int = 0
   137→        self.filter_engine = MetadataFilterEngine()  # Initialize filter engine
   138→
   139→        # Derive index base name for standard sibling fallbacks, e.g., <index_name>.passages.*
   140→        index_name_base = None
   141→        if metadata_file_path:
   142→            meta_name = Path(metadata_file_path).name
   143→            if meta_name.endswith(".meta.json"):
   144→                index_name_base = meta_name[: -len(".meta.json")]
   145→
   146→        for source in passage_sources:
   147→            assert source["type"] == "jsonl", "only jsonl is supported"
   148→            passage_file = source.get("path", "")
   149→            index_file = source.get("index_path", "")  # .idx file
   150→
   151→            # Fix path resolution - relative paths should be relative to metadata file directory
   152→            def _resolve_candidates(
   153→                primary: str,
   154→                relative_key: str,
   155→                default_name: Optional[str],
   156→                source_dict: dict[str, Any],
   157→            ) -> list[Path]:
   158→                """
   159→                Build an ordered list of candidate paths. For relative paths specified in
   160→                metadata, prefer resolution relative to the metadata file directory first,
   161→                then fall back to CWD-based resolution, and finally to conventional
   162→                sibling defaults (e.g., <index_base>.passages.idx / .jsonl).
   163→                """
   164→                candidates: list[Path] = []
   165→                # 1) Primary path
   166→                if primary:
   167→                    p = Path(primary)
   168→                    if p.is_absolute():
   169→                        candidates.append(p)
   170→                    else:
   171→                        # Prefer metadata-relative resolution for relative paths
   172→                        if metadata_file_path:
   173→                            candidates.append(Path(metadata_file_path).parent / p)
   174→                        # Also consider CWD-relative as a fallback for legacy layouts
   175→                        candidates.append(Path.cwd() / p)
   176→                # 2) metadata-relative explicit relative key (if present)
   177→                if metadata_file_path and source_dict.get(relative_key):
   178→                    candidates.append(Path(metadata_file_path).parent / source_dict[relative_key])
   179→                # 3) metadata-relative standard sibling filename
   180→                if metadata_file_path and default_name:
   181→                    candidates.append(Path(metadata_file_path).parent / default_name)
   182→                return candidates
   183→
   184→            # Build candidate lists and pick first existing; otherwise keep last candidate for error message
   185→            idx_default = f"{index_name_base}.passages.idx" if index_name_base else None
   186→            idx_candidates = _resolve_candidates(
   187→                index_file, "index_path_relative", idx_default, source
   188→            )
   189→            pas_default = f"{index_name_base}.passages.jsonl" if index_name_base else None
   190→            pas_candidates = _resolve_candidates(passage_file, "path_relative", pas_default, source)
   191→
   192→            def _pick_existing(cands: list[Path]) -> str:
   193→                for c in cands:
   194→                    if c.exists():
   195→                        return str(c.resolve())
   196→                # Fallback to last candidate (best guess) even if not exists; will error below
   197→                return str(cands[-1].resolve()) if cands else ""
   198→
   199→            index_file = _pick_existing(idx_candidates)
   200→            passage_file = _pick_existing(pas_candidates)
   201→
   202→            if not Path(index_file).exists():
   203→                raise FileNotFoundError(f"Passage index file not found: {index_file}")
   204→
   205→            with open(index_file, "rb") as f:
   206→                offset_map: dict[str, int] = pickle.load(f)
   207→                self.offset_maps[passage_file] = offset_map
   208→                self.passage_files[passage_file] = passage_file
   209→                self._total_count += len(offset_map)
   210→
   211→    def get_passage(self, passage_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
   212→        # Fast path: check each shard map (there are typically few shards).
   213→        # This avoids building a massive combined dict while keeping lookups
   214→        # bounded by the number of shards.
   215→        for passage_file, offset_map in self.offset_maps.items():
   216→            try:
   217→                offset = offset_map[passage_id]
   218→                with open(passage_file, encoding="utf-8") as f:
   219→                    f.seek(offset)
   220→                    return json.loads(f.readline())
   221→            except KeyError:
   222→                continue
   223→        raise KeyError(f"Passage ID not found: {passage_id}")
   224→
   225→    def filter_search_results(
   226→        self,
   227→        search_results: list[SearchResult],
   228→        metadata_filters: Optional[dict[str, dict[str, Union[str, int, float, bool, list]]]],
   229→    ) -> list[SearchResult]:
   230→        """
   231→        Apply metadata filters to search results.
   232→
   233→        Args:
   234→            search_results: List of SearchResult objects
   235→            metadata_filters: Filter specifications to apply
   236→
   237→        Returns:
   238→            Filtered list of SearchResult objects
   239→        """
   240→        if not metadata_filters:
   241→            return search_results
   242→
   243→        logger.debug(f"Applying metadata filters to {len(search_results)} results")
   244→
   245→        # Convert SearchResult objects to dictionaries for the filter engine
   246→        result_dicts = []
   247→        for result in search_results:
   248→            result_dicts.append(
   249→                {
   250→                    "id": result.id,
   251→                    "score": result.score,
   252→                    "text": result.text,
   253→                    "metadata": result.metadata,
   254→                }
   255→            )
   256→
   257→        # Apply filters using the filter engine
   258→        filtered_dicts = self.filter_engine.apply_filters(result_dicts, metadata_filters)
   259→
   260→        # Convert back to SearchResult objects
   261→        filtered_results = []
   262→        for result_dict in filtered_dicts:
   263→            filtered_results.append(
   264→                SearchResult(
   265→                    id=result_dict["id"],
   266→                    score=result_dict["score"],
   267→                    text=result_dict["text"],
   268→                    metadata=result_dict["metadata"],
   269→                )
   270→            )
   271→
   272→        logger.debug(f"Filtered results: {len(filtered_results)} remaining")
   273→        return filtered_results
   274→
   275→    def __len__(self) -> int:
   276→        return self._total_count

   279→class LeannBuilder:
   280→    def __init__(
   281→        self,
   282→        backend_name: str,
   283→        embedding_model: str = "facebook/contriever",
   284→        dimensions: Optional[int] = None,
   285→        embedding_mode: str = "sentence-transformers",
   286→        embedding_options: Optional[dict[str, Any]] = None,
   287→        **backend_kwargs,
   288→    ):
   289→        self.backend_name = backend_name
   290→        # Normalize incompatible combinations early (for consistent metadata)
   291→        if backend_name == "hnsw":
   292→            is_recompute = backend_kwargs.get("is_recompute", True)
   293→            is_compact = backend_kwargs.get("is_compact", True)
   294→            if is_recompute is False and is_compact is True:
   295→                warnings.warn(
   296→                    "HNSW with is_recompute=False requires non-compact storage. Forcing is_compact=False.",
   297→                    UserWarning,
   298→                    stacklevel=2,
   299→                )
   300→                backend_kwargs["is_compact"] = False
   301→
   302→        backend_factory: Optional[LeannBackendFactoryInterface] = BACKEND_REGISTRY.get(backend_name)
   303→        if backend_factory is None:
   304→            raise ValueError(f"Backend '{backend_name}' not found or not registered.")
   305→        self.backend_factory = backend_factory
   306→        self.embedding_model = embedding_model
   307→        self.dimensions = dimensions
   308→        self.embedding_mode = embedding_mode
   309→        self.embedding_options = embedding_options or {}
   310→
   311→        # Check if we need to use cosine distance for normalized embeddings
   312→        normalized_embeddings_models = {
   313→            # OpenAI models
   314→            ("openai", "text-embedding-ada-002"),
   315→            ("openai", "text-embedding-3-small"),
   316→            ("openai", "text-embedding-3-large"),
   317→            # Voyage AI models
   318→            ("voyage", "voyage-2"),
   319→            ("voyage", "voyage-3"),
   320→            ("voyage", "voyage-large-2"),
   321→            ("voyage", "voyage-multilingual-2"),
   322→            ("voyage", "voyage-code-2"),
   323→            # Cohere models
   324→            ("cohere", "embed-english-v3.0"),
   325→            ("cohere", "embed-multilingual-v3.0"),
   326→            ("cohere", "embed-english-light-v3.0"),
   327→            ("cohere", "embed-multilingual-light-v3.0"),
   328→        }
   329→
   330→        # Also check for patterns in model names
   331→        is_normalized = False
   332→        current_model_lower = embedding_model.lower()
   333→        current_mode_lower = embedding_mode.lower()
   334→
   335→        # Check exact matches
   336→        for mode, model in normalized_embeddings_models:
   337→            if (current_mode_lower == mode and current_model_lower == model) or (
   338→                mode in current_mode_lower and model in current_model_lower
   339→            ):
   340→                is_normalized = True
   341→                break
   342→
   343→        # Check patterns
   344→        if not is_normalized:
   345→            # OpenAI patterns
   346→            if "openai" in current_mode_lower or "openai" in current_model_lower:
   347→                if any(
   348→                    pattern in current_model_lower
   349→                    for pattern in ["text-embedding", "ada", "3-small", "3-large"]
   350→                ):
   351→                    is_normalized = True
   352→            # Voyage patterns
   353→            elif "voyage" in current_mode_lower or "voyage" in current_model_lower:
   354→                is_normalized = True
   355→            # Cohere patterns
   356→            elif "cohere" in current_mode_lower or "cohere" in current_model_lower:
   357→                if "embed" in current_model_lower:
   358→                    is_normalized = True
   359→
   360→        # Handle distance metric
   361→        if is_normalized and "distance_metric" not in backend_kwargs:
   362→            backend_kwargs["distance_metric"] = "cosine"
   363→            warnings.warn(
   364→                f"Detected normalized embeddings model '{embedding_model}' with mode '{embedding_mode}'. "
   365→                f"Automatically setting distance_metric='cosine' for optimal performance. "
   366→                f"Normalized embeddings (L2 norm = 1) should use cosine similarity instead of MIPS.",
   367→                UserWarning,
   368→                stacklevel=2,
   369→            )
   370→        elif is_normalized and backend_kwargs.get("distance_metric", "").lower() != "cosine":
   371→            current_metric = backend_kwargs.get("distance_metric", "mips")
   372→            warnings.warn(
   373→                f"Warning: Using '{current_metric}' distance metric with normalized embeddings model "
   374→                f"'{embedding_model}' may lead to suboptimal search results. "
   375→                f"Consider using 'cosine' distance metric for better performance.",
   376→                UserWarning,
   377→                stacklevel=2,
   378→            )
   379→
   380→        self.backend_kwargs = backend_kwargs
   381→        self.chunks: list[dict[str, Any]] = []

   383→    def add_text(self, text: str, metadata: Optional[dict[str, Any]] = None):

   390→    def build_index(self, index_path: str):
   391→        if not self.chunks:

   393→
   394→        # Filter out invalid/empty text chunks early to keep passage and embedding counts aligned
   395→        valid_chunks: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
   396→        skipped = 0
   397→        for chunk in self.chunks:
   398→            text = chunk.get("text", "")
   399→            if isinstance(text, str) and text.strip():
   400→                valid_chunks.append(chunk)
   401→            else:
   402→                skipped += 1
   403→        if skipped > 0:
   404→            print(
   405→                f"Warning: Skipping {skipped} empty/invalid text chunk(s). Processing {len(valid_chunks)} valid chunks"
   406→            )
   407→            self.chunks = valid_chunks
   408→            if not self.chunks:
   409→                raise ValueError("All provided chunks are empty or invalid. Nothing to index.")
   410→        if self.dimensions is None:
   411→            self.dimensions = len(
   412→                compute_embeddings(
   413→                    ["dummy"],
   414→                    self.embedding_model,

   420→        path = Path(index_path)

   425→        offset_file = index_dir / f"{index_name}.passages.idx"

   428→            try:

   431→                chunk_iterator = tqdm(self.chunks, desc="Writing passages", unit="chunk")
   432→            except ImportError:

   434→
   435→            for chunk in chunk_iterator:
   436→                offset = f.tell()
   437→                json.dump(
   438→                    {
   439→                        "id": chunk["id"],
   440→                        "text": chunk["text"],
   441→                        "metadata": chunk["metadata"],
   442→                    },
   443→                    f,
   444→                    ensure_ascii=False,
   445→                )
   446→                f.write("\n")
   447→                offset_map[chunk["id"]] = offset
   448→        with open(offset_file, "wb") as f:
   449→            pickle.dump(offset_map, f)
   450→        texts_to_embed = [c["text"] for c in self.chunks]
   451→        embeddings = compute_embeddings(

   466→            with open(idmap_file, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:

   472→        builder_instance = self.backend_factory.builder(**current_backend_kwargs)
   473→        builder_instance.build(embeddings, string_ids, index_path, **current_backend_kwargs)
   474→        leann_meta_path = index_dir / f"{index_name}.meta.json"
   475→        meta_data = {

   489→                    "path_relative": passages_file.name,

   495→        if self.embedding_options:

   498→        # Add storage status flags for HNSW backend

   507→    def build_index_from_embeddings(self, index_path: str, embeddings_file: str):
   508→        """
   509→        Build an index from pre-computed embeddings stored in a pickle file.
   510→
   511→        Args:
   512→            index_path: Path where the index will be saved
   513→            embeddings_file: Path to pickle file containing (ids, embeddings) tuple
   514→        """
   515→        # Load pre-computed embeddings
   516→        with open(embeddings_file, "rb") as f:
   517→            data = pickle.load(f)
   518→
   519→        if not isinstance(data, tuple) or len(data) != 2:
   520→            raise ValueError(
   521→                f"Invalid embeddings file format. Expected tuple with 2 elements, got {type(data)}"
   522→            )
   523→
   524→        ids, embeddings = data
   525→
   526→        if not isinstance(embeddings, np.ndarray):
   527→            raise ValueError(f"Expected embeddings to be numpy array, got {type(embeddings)}")
   528→
   529→        if len(ids) != embeddings.shape[0]:
   530→            raise ValueError(
   531→                f"Mismatch between number of IDs ({len(ids)}) and embeddings ({embeddings.shape[0]})"
   532→            )
   533→
   534→        # Validate/set dimensions
   535→        embedding_dim = embeddings.shape[1]
   536→        if self.dimensions is None:
   537→            self.dimensions = embedding_dim
   538→        elif self.dimensions != embedding_dim:
   539→            raise ValueError(f"Dimension mismatch: expected {self.dimensions}, got {embedding_dim}")
   540→
   541→        logger.info(
   542→            f"Building index from precomputed embeddings: {len(ids)} items, {embedding_dim} dimensions"
   543→        )
   544→
   545→        # Ensure we have text data for each embedding
   546→        if len(self.chunks) != len(ids):
   547→            # If no text chunks provided, create placeholder text entries
   548→            if not self.chunks:
   549→                logger.info("No text chunks provided, creating placeholder entries...")
   550→                for id_val in ids:
   551→                    self.add_text(
   552→                        f"Document {id_val}",
   553→                        metadata={"id": str(id_val), "from_embeddings": True},
   554→                    )
   555→            else:
   556→                raise ValueError(
   557→                    f"Number of text chunks ({len(self.chunks)}) doesn't match number of embeddings ({len(ids)})"
   558→                )
   559→
   560→        # Build file structure
   561→        path = Path(index_path)
   562→        index_dir = path.parent
   563→        index_name = path.name
   564→        index_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   565→        passages_file = index_dir / f"{index_name}.passages.jsonl"
   566→        offset_file = index_dir / f"{index_name}.passages.idx"
   567→
   568→        # Write passages and create offset map
   569→        offset_map = {}
   570→        with open(passages_file, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
   571→            for chunk in self.chunks:
   572→                offset = f.tell()
   573→                json.dump(
   574→                    {
   575→                        "id": chunk["id"],
   576→                        "text": chunk["text"],
   577→                        "metadata": chunk["metadata"],
   578→                    },
   579→                    f,
   580→                    ensure_ascii=False,
   581→                )
   582→                f.write("\n")
   583→                offset_map[chunk["id"]] = offset
   584→
   585→        with open(offset_file, "wb") as f:
   586→            pickle.dump(offset_map, f)
   587→
   588→        # Build the vector index using precomputed embeddings
   589→        string_ids = [str(id_val) for id_val in ids]
   590→        # Persist ID map (order == embeddings order)
   591→        try:
   592→            idmap_file = (
   593→                index_dir
   594→                / f"{index_name[: -len('.leann')] if index_name.endswith('.leann') else index_name}.ids.txt"
   595→            )
   596→            with open(idmap_file, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
   597→                for sid in string_ids:
   598→                    f.write(str(sid) + "\n")
   599→        except Exception:
   600→            pass
   601→        current_backend_kwargs = {**self.backend_kwargs, "dimensions": self.dimensions}
   602→        builder_instance = self.backend_factory.builder(**current_backend_kwargs)

   660→            raise FileNotFoundError("Index metadata or passage files are missing; cannot update.")
   661→        if not index_file.exists():
   662→            raise FileNotFoundError(f"HNSW index file not found: {index_file}")
   663→

   665→            meta = json.load(f)
   666→        backend_name = meta.get("backend_name")
   667→        if backend_name != self.backend_name:

   670→            )

import json
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional


def batch_get_passages(
    index_path: str,
    passage_ids: List[str]
) -> Dict[str, Optional[Dict[str, Any]]]:
    """Retrieve multiple passages by their IDs from a index.

    Args:
        index_path: Path to the index file
        passage_ids: List of passage IDs to retrieve

    Returns:
        Dictionary mapping passage_id to passage data (id, text, metadata).
        Missing passages will have None as value.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: If index metadata file is not found
    """
    # Import PassageManager from the leann library
    from leann.api import PassageManager

    # Construct the metadata file path
    # The index_path should point to the .leann file, and metadata is .leann.meta.json
    meta_path = f"{index_path}.meta.json"

    # Check if metadata file exists
    if not Path(meta_path).exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Index metadata file not found: {meta_path}")

    # Load the index metadata
    with open(meta_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        meta_data = json.load(f)

    # Get passage sources from metadata
    passage_sources = meta_data.get("passage_sources", [])

    # Create PassageManager instance
    passage_manager = PassageManager(
        passage_sources=passage_sources,
        metadata_file_path=meta_path
    )

    # Retrieve passages for each ID
    result: Dict[str, Optional[Dict[str, Any]]] = {}

    for passage_id in passage_ids:
        try:
            # Attempt to retrieve the passage
            passage_data = passage_manager.get_passage(passage_id)
            result[passage_id] = passage_data
        except KeyError:
            # Handle missing passages gracefully by setting to None
            result[passage_id] = None

    return result

        passage_ids: List of passage IDs to retrieve
        
    Returns:
        Dictionary mapping passage_id to passage data (id, text, metadata).
        Missing passages will have None as value.
        
    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: If index metadata file is not found
    """
    # Import PassageManager from the leann library
    from leann.api import PassageManager
    
    # Construct the metadata file path
    # The index_path should point to the .leann file, and metadata is .leann.meta.json
    meta_path = f"{index_path}.meta.json"
    
    # Check if metadata file exists
    if not Path(meta_path).exists():

    # Load the index metadata
    with open(meta_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        meta_data = json.load(f)
    
    # Get passage sources from metadata
    passage_sources = meta_data.get("passage_sources", [])
    
    # Create PassageManager instance
    passage_manager = PassageManager(
        passage_sources=passage_sources,
        metadata_file_path=meta_path
    )
    
    # Retrieve passages for each ID
    result: Dict[str, Optional[Dict[str, Any]]] = {}
    
    for passage_id in passage_ids:
        try:
            # Attempt to retrieve the passage
            passage_data = passage_manager.get_passage(passage_id)
            result[passage_id] = passage_data
        except KeyError:
            # Handle missing passages gracefully by setting to None
            result[passage_id] = None

from typing import List, Dict, Any, Optional
from leann.cli import LeannCLI
from leann.api import LeannBuilder, LeannSearcher
from pathlib import Path


def parse_and_build_index_from_cli_args(
    args_list: List[str],
    output_index_path: Optional[str] = None
) -> str:
    """Parse CLI build arguments and execute index building via API.
    
    Args:
        args_list: List of command line arguments, starting with 'build' command.
            Example: ["build", "my-index", "--docs", "./docs", "--backend-name", "hnsw"]
        output_index_path: Optional custom output path. If None, uses CLI default location.
        
    Returns:
        Path to the built index file
        
    Raises:
        ValueError: If args_list doesn't start with 'build' or if required arguments are missing
    """
    if not args_list or args_list[0] != "build":
        raise ValueError("args_list must start with 'build' command")
    
    # Create CLI parser
    cli = LeannCLI()
    parser = cli.create_parser()
    
    # Parse arguments
    args = parser.parse_args(args_list)
    
    # Validate parsed arguments
    if args.command != "build":
        raise ValueError(f"Expected 'build' command, got '{args.command}'")
    
    # Determine index path
    if output_index_path:
        index_path = output_index_path
    else:
        # Use CLI's default path logic
        index_name = args.index_name if args.index_name else Path.cwd().name
        index_path = cli.get_index_path(index_name)
        # Ensure parent directory exists
        Path(index_path).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    
    # Extract build parameters
    backend_name = args.backend_name
    docs_paths = args.docs
    
    # Build index using API (not CLI async method)
    builder = LeannBuilder(backend_name=backend_name)
    
    # Load documents using CLI's document loading method
    # Note: args should be the parsed argparse.Namespace object
    all_texts = cli.load_documents(
        docs_paths=docs_paths,
        custom_file_types=getattr(args, 'file_types', None),
        include_hidden=getattr(args, 'include_hidden', False),
        args=args
    )
    
    if not all_texts:
        raise ValueError("No documents found to index")
    
    # Add all texts to builder
    for chunk in all_texts:
        text = chunk.get("text", "")
        metadata = chunk.get("metadata", {})
        builder.add_text(text, metadata=metadata)
    
    # Build the index
    builder.build_index(index_path)
    
    return index_path


def parse_and_search_from_cli_args(
    args_list: List[str]
) -> List[Any]:
    """Parse CLI search arguments and execute search via API.
    
    Args:
        args_list: List of command line arguments, starting with 'search' command.
            Example: ["search", "my-index", "python programming", "--top-k", "10"]
        
    Returns:
        List of SearchResult objects
        
    Raises:
        ValueError: If args_list doesn't start with 'search' or if required arguments are missing
    """
    if not args_list or args_list[0] != "search":
        raise ValueError("args_list must start with 'search' command")
    
    # Create CLI parser
    cli = LeannCLI()
    parser = cli.create_parser()
    
    # Parse arguments - catch SystemExit from argparse when required arguments are missing
    import sys
    try:
        args = parser.parse_args(args_list)
    except SystemExit as e:
        # argparse calls sys.exit(2) when required arguments are missing
        # Convert this to ValueError for better error handling
        if e.code == 2:
            raise ValueError("query is required for search command") from None
        raise
    
    # Validate parsed arguments
    if args.command != "search":
        raise ValueError(f"Expected 'search' command, got '{args.command}'")
    
    if not args.index_name:
        raise ValueError("index_name is required for search command")
    # Check if query is None or empty string
    if not hasattr(args, 'query') or args.query is None or (isinstance(args.query, str) and not args.query.strip()):
        raise ValueError("query is required for search command")
    
    # Get index path
    index_path = cli.get_index_path(args.index_name)
    
    if not cli.index_exists(args.index_name):
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Index '{args.index_name}' not found at {index_path}")
    
    # Create searcher and perform search
    searcher = LeannSearcher(index_path=index_path)
    
    results = searcher.search(
        query=args.query,
        top_k=args.top_k,
        complexity=args.complexity if hasattr(args, 'complexity') else 64
    )
    
    return results

    def build_index(self, index_path: str):
        if not self.chunks:
            raise ValueError("No chunks added.")

        # Filter out invalid/empty text chunks early to keep passage and embedding counts aligned
        valid_chunks: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        skipped = 0
        for chunk in self.chunks:
            text = chunk.get("text", "")
            if isinstance(text, str) and text.strip():
                valid_chunks.append(chunk)
            else:
                skipped += 1
        if skipped > 0:
            print(
                f"Warning: Skipping {skipped} empty/invalid text chunk(s). Processing {len(valid_chunks)} valid chunks"
            )
            self.chunks = valid_chunks
            if not self.chunks:
                raise ValueError("All provided chunks are empty or invalid. Nothing to index.")
        if self.dimensions is None:
            self.dimensions = len(
                compute_embeddings(
                    ["dummy"],
                    self.embedding_model,
                    self.embedding_mode,
                    use_server=False,
                    provider_options=self.embedding_options,
                )[0]
            )
        path = Path(index_path)
        index_dir = path.parent
        index_name = path.name
        index_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        passages_file = index_dir / f"{index_name}.passages.jsonl"
        offset_file = index_dir / f"{index_name}.passages.idx"
        offset_map = {}
        with open(passages_file, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            try:
                from tqdm import tqdm

                chunk_iterator = tqdm(self.chunks, desc="Writing passages", unit="chunk")
            except ImportError:
                chunk_iterator = self.chunks

            for chunk in chunk_iterator:
                offset = f.tell()
                json.dump(
                    {
                        "id": chunk["id"],
                        "text": chunk["text"],
                        "metadata": chunk["metadata"],
                    },
                    f,
                    ensure_ascii=False,
                )
                f.write("\n")
                offset_map[chunk["id"]] = offset
        with open(offset_file, "wb") as f:
            pickle.dump(offset_map, f)
        texts_to_embed = [c["text"] for c in self.chunks]
        embeddings = compute_embeddings(
            texts_to_embed,
            self.embedding_model,
            self.embedding_mode,
            use_server=False,
            is_build=True,
            provider_options=self.embedding_options,
        )
        string_ids = [chunk["id"] for chunk in self.chunks]
        # Persist ID map alongside index so backends that return integer labels can remap to passage IDs
        try:
            idmap_file = (
                index_dir
                / f"{index_name[: -len('.leann')] if index_name.endswith('.leann') else index_name}.ids.txt"
            )
            with open(idmap_file, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                for sid in string_ids:
                    f.write(str(sid) + "\n")
        except Exception:
            pass
        current_backend_kwargs = {**self.backend_kwargs, "dimensions": self.dimensions}
        builder_instance = self.backend_factory.builder(**current_backend_kwargs)
        builder_instance.build(embeddings, string_ids, index_path, **current_backend_kwargs)
        leann_meta_path = index_dir / f"{index_name}.meta.json"
        meta_data = {
            "version": "1.0",
            "backend_name": self.backend_name,
            "embedding_model": self.embedding_model,
            "dimensions": self.dimensions,
            "backend_kwargs": self.backend_kwargs,
            "embedding_mode": self.embedding_mode,

                    # Preserve existing relative file names (backward-compatible)

                    # Add optional redundant relative keys for remote build portability (non-breaking)
                    "path_relative": passages_file.name,

            is_recompute = self.backend_kwargs.get("is_recompute", True)

        if not Path(self.meta_path_str).exists():
            parent_dir = Path(index_path).parent
            print(
                f"Leann metadata file not found at {self.meta_path_str}, and you may need to rm -rf {parent_dir}"

            )
        with open(self.meta_path_str, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            self.meta_data = json.load(f)
        backend_name = self.meta_data["backend_name"]
        self.embedding_model = self.meta_data["embedding_model"]
        # Support both old and new format
        self.embedding_mode = self.meta_data.get("embedding_mode", "sentence-transformers")

        # Delegate portability handling to PassageManager

            complexity: Search complexity/candidate list size, higher = more accurate but slower
            beam_width: Number of parallel search paths/IO requests per iteration
            prune_ratio: Ratio of neighbors to prune via approximate distance (0.0-1.0)
            recompute_embeddings: Whether to fetch fresh embeddings from server vs use stored codes
            pruning_strategy: Candidate selection strategy - "global" (default), "local", or "proportional"
            expected_zmq_port: ZMQ port for embedding server communication
            metadata_filters: Optional filters to apply to search results based on metadata.
                Format: {"field_name": {"operator": value}}
                Supported operators:
                - Comparison: "==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">="
                - Membership: "in", "not_in"
                - String: "contains", "starts_with", "ends_with"
                Example: {"chapter": {"<=": 5}, "tags": {"in": ["fiction", "drama"]}}
            **kwargs: Backend-specific parameters

        Returns:

        """

            return self._grep_search(query, top_k)

        logger.info("🔍 LeannSearcher.search() called:")

        logger.info(f"  Top_k: {top_k}")
        logger.info(f"  Metadata filters: {metadata_filters}")
        logger.info(f"  Additional kwargs: {kwargs}")

        # Smart top_k detection and adjustment
        # Use PassageManager length (sum of shard sizes) to avoid
        # depending on a massive combined map
        total_docs = len(self.passage_manager)
        original_top_k = top_k
        if top_k > total_docs:
            top_k = total_docs
            logger.warning(
                f"  ⚠️  Requested top_k ({original_top_k}) exceeds total documents ({total_docs})"
            )
            logger.warning(f"  ✅ Auto-adjusted top_k to {top_k} to match available documents")

        zmq_port = None

        start_time = time.time()
        if recompute_embeddings:
            zmq_port = self.backend_impl._ensure_server_running(
                self.meta_path_str,
                port=expected_zmq_port,
                **kwargs,
            )
            del expected_zmq_port
        zmq_time = time.time() - start_time
        logger.info(f"  Launching server time: {zmq_time} seconds")

        start_time = time.time()

        query_embedding = self.backend_impl.compute_query_embedding(

            zmq_port=zmq_port,
        )
        logger.info(f"  Generated embedding shape: {query_embedding.shape}")
        embedding_time = time.time() - start_time
        logger.info(f"  Embedding time: {embedding_time} seconds")

        start_time = time.time()
        backend_search_kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {
            "complexity": complexity,
            "beam_width": beam_width,
            "prune_ratio": prune_ratio,
            "recompute_embeddings": recompute_embeddings,
            "pruning_strategy": pruning_strategy,
            "zmq_port": zmq_port,
        }
        # Only HNSW supports batching; forward conditionally
        if self.backend_name == "hnsw":
            backend_search_kwargs["batch_size"] = batch_size

        # Merge any extra kwargs last
        backend_search_kwargs.update(kwargs)

        results = self.backend_impl.search(
            query_embedding,
            top_k,
            **backend_search_kwargs,
        )
        search_time = time.time() - start_time
        logger.info(f"  Search time in search() LEANN searcher: {search_time} seconds")
        logger.info(f"  Backend returned: labels={len(results.get('labels', [[]])[0])} results")

        enriched_results = []
        if "labels" in results and "distances" in results:
            logger.info(f"  Processing {len(results['labels'][0])} passage IDs:")
            # Python 3.9 does not support zip(strict=...); lengths are expected to match
            for i, (string_id, dist) in enumerate(
                zip(results["labels"][0], results["distances"][0])
            ):
                try:
                    passage_data = self.passage_manager.get_passage(string_id)
                    enriched_results.append(
                        SearchResult(
                            id=string_id,
                            score=dist,
                            text=passage_data["text"],
                            metadata=passage_data.get("metadata", {}),
                        )
                    )

                    # Color codes for better logging
                    GREEN = "\033[92m"
                    BLUE = "\033[94m"
                    YELLOW = "\033[93m"
                    RESET = "\033[0m"

                    # Truncate text for display (first 100 chars)
                    display_text = passage_data["text"]
                    logger.info(
                        f"   {GREEN}✓{RESET} {BLUE}[{i + 1:2d}]{RESET} {YELLOW}ID:{RESET} '{string_id}' {YELLOW}Score:{RESET} {dist:.4f} {YELLOW}Text:{RESET} {display_text}"
                    )
                except KeyError:
                    RED = "\033[91m"
                    RESET = "\033[0m"
                    logger.error(
                        f"   {RED}✗{RESET} [{i + 1:2d}] ID: '{string_id}' -> {RED}ERROR: Passage not found!{RESET}"
                    )

        # Apply metadata filters if specified
        if metadata_filters:
            logger.info(f"  🔍 Applying metadata filters: {metadata_filters}")
            enriched_results = self.passage_manager.filter_search_results(
                enriched_results, metadata_filters
            )

        # Define color codes outside the loop for final message
        GREEN = "\033[92m"
        RESET = "\033[0m"
        logger.info(f"  {GREEN}✓ Final enriched results: {len(enriched_results)} passages{RESET}")
        return enriched_results

# Implementation Plan: CLI Argument Parsing Functions

## Context

The user needs two functions to programmatically interact with the LEANN CLI (a vector index search library) by parsing command-line arguments and executing the corresponding build/search operations. This is useful for:
- Automating index building and searching from Python code
- Testing CLI functionality programmatically
- Building workflows that need to invoke CLI operations without subprocess calls

The functions should parse arguments from a list of strings (simulating command-line input), validate them, and execute the appropriate operations using LEANN's existing API classes.

## Critical Files

- `/data/workspace/AgenticSearch/total_third_party_projects/LEANN/packages/leann-core/src/leann/cli.py` - Main CLI implementation with LeannCLI class
- `/data/workspace/AgenticSearch/total_third_party_projects/LEANN/packages/leann-core/src/leann/api.py` - Core API with LeannBuilder and LeannSearcher classes

## Implementation Approach

### Function 1: `parse_and_build_index_from_cli_args`

This function will:
1. **Validate command**: Check that args_list starts with 'build', raise ValueError if not
2. **Parse arguments**: Use LeannCLI's existing argparse parser to parse the args_list
3. **Load documents**: Use LeannCLI's `load_documents()` method with parsed paths and options
4. **Build index**: Create a LeannBuilder instance with parsed configuration (backend, model, etc.)
5. **Save index**: Use output_index_path if provided, otherwise use LeannCLI's `get_index_path()` logic
6. **Return path**: Return the path to the built index file

Key considerations:
- Reuse LeannCLI's existing parser via `create_parser()`
- Leverage existing `load_documents()` method for document loading with gitignore support
- Use LeannBuilder API for index building
- Handle both custom output path and default CLI path logic

### Function 2: `parse_and_search_from_cli_args`

This function will:
1. **Validate command**: Check that args_list starts with 'search', raise ValueError if not
2. **Validate query**: Check that query argument is present, raise ValueError with specific message if not
3. **Parse arguments**: Use LeannCLI's existing argparse parser
4. **Verify index exists**: Check that the index exists at the expected path, raise ValueError with "not found" message if not
5. **Execute search**: Create LeannSearcher instance and execute search with parsed parameters
6. **Return results**: Return list of SearchResult objects

Key considerations:
- Reuse LeannCLI's existing parser
- Use LeannCLI's `get_index_path()` and `index_exists()` methods
- Use LeannSearcher API for searching
- Handle search parameters: top_k, complexity, beam_width, prune_ratio, etc.

## Implementation Details

### Shared Utilities
Both functions will:
- Import LeannCLI and instantiate it to access parser and helper methods
- Use LeannCLI.create_parser() to get the argparse parser
- Parse args_list using parser.parse_args(args_list)
- Access parsed arguments via the returned namespace object

### Document Loading (for build function)
- Call `cli.load_documents()` with:
  - docs_paths from args.docs
  - custom_file_types from args.file_types
  - include_hidden from args.include_hidden
  - Pass args object for AST chunking options

### Index Building
- Create LeannBuilder with:
  - backend_name, embedding_model, embedding_mode from args
  - embedding_options dict constructed from args (host, api_base, api_key, templates)
  - backend_kwargs: graph_degree, complexity, compact, recompute, num_threads
- Add texts from loaded documents with metadata
- Call builder.build_index(index_path)

### Index Path Resolution
- If output_index_path provided, use it directly
- Otherwise, determine index_name from args.index_name or Path.cwd().name
- Use cli.get_index_path(index_name) for default location

### Search Execution
- Verify index exists using cli.index_exists() or check file existence
- Create LeannSearcher with index_path
- Execute search with query and parameters from args
- Return list of SearchResult objects

   415→    def _build_gitignore_parser(self, docs_dir: str):
   416→        """Build gitignore parser using gitignore-parser library."""
   417→        from gitignore_parser import parse_gitignore
   418→
   419→        # Try to parse the root .gitignore
   420→        gitignore_path = Path(docs_dir) / ".gitignore"
   421→
   422→        if gitignore_path.exists():
   423→            try:
   424→                # gitignore-parser automatically handles all subdirectory .gitignore files!
   425→                matches = parse_gitignore(str(gitignore_path))
   426→                print(f"📋 Loaded .gitignore from {docs_dir} (includes all subdirectories)")
   427→                return matches
   428→            except Exception as e:
   429→                print(f"Warning: Could not parse .gitignore: {e}")
   430→        else:
   431→            print("📋 No .gitignore found")
   432→
   433→        # Fallback: basic pattern matching for essential files
   434→        essential_patterns = {".git", ".DS_Store", "__pycache__", "node_modules", ".venv", "venv"}
   435→
   436→        def basic_matches(file_path):
   437→            path_parts = Path(file_path).parts
   438→            return any(part in essential_patterns for part in path_parts)
   439→
   440→        return basic_matches

   442→    def _should_exclude_file(self, file_path: Path, gitignore_matches) -> bool:
   443→        """Check if a file should be excluded using gitignore parser.
   444→
   445→        Always match against absolute, posix-style paths for consistency with
   446→        gitignore_parser expectations.
   447→        """
   448→        try:
   449→            absolute_path = file_path.resolve()
   450→        except Exception:
   451→            absolute_path = Path(str(file_path))
   452→        return gitignore_matches(absolute_path.as_posix())

   454→    def _is_git_submodule(self, path: Path) -> bool:
   455→        """Check if a path is a git submodule."""
   456→        try:
   457→            # Find the git repo root
   458→            current_dir = Path.cwd()
   459→            while current_dir != current_dir.parent:
   460→                if (current_dir / ".git").exists():
   461→                    gitmodules_path = current_dir / ".gitmodules"
   462→                    if gitmodules_path.exists():
   463→                        # Read .gitmodules to check if this path is a submodule
   464→                        gitmodules_content = gitmodules_path.read_text()
   465→                        # Convert path to relative to git root
   466→                        try:
   467→                            relative_path = path.resolve().relative_to(current_dir)
   468→                            # Check if this path appears in .gitmodules
   469→                            return f"path = {relative_path}" in gitmodules_content
   470→                        except ValueError:
   471→                            # Path is not under git root
   472→                            return False
   473→                    break
   474→                current_dir = current_dir.parent
   475→            return False
   476→        except Exception:
   477→            # If anything goes wrong, assume it's not a submodule
   478→            return False

   589→    def _discover_indexes_in_project(
   590→        self, project_path: Path, exclude_dirs: Optional[list[Path]] = None
   591→    ):
   592→        """Discover all indexes in a project directory (both CLI and apps formats)
   593→
   594→        exclude_dirs: when provided, skip any APP-format index files that are
   595→        located under these directories. This prevents duplicates when the
   596→        current project is a parent directory of other registered projects.
   597→        """
   598→        indexes = []
   599→        exclude_dirs = exclude_dirs or []
   600→        # normalize to resolved paths once for comparison
   601→        try:
   602→            exclude_dirs_resolved = [p.resolve() for p in exclude_dirs]
   603→        except Exception:
   604→            exclude_dirs_resolved = exclude_dirs
   605→
   606→        # 1. CLI format: .leann/indexes/index_name/
   607→        cli_indexes_dir = project_path / ".leann" / "indexes"
   608→        if cli_indexes_dir.exists():
   609→            for index_dir in cli_indexes_dir.iterdir():
   610→                if index_dir.is_dir():
   611→                    meta_file = index_dir / "documents.leann.meta.json"
   612→                    status = "✅" if meta_file.exists() else "❌"
   613→
   614→                    size_mb = 0
   615→                    if meta_file.exists():
   616→                        try:
   617→                            size_mb = sum(
   618→                                f.stat().st_size for f in index_dir.iterdir() if f.is_file()
   619→                            ) / (1024 * 1024)
   620→                        except (OSError, PermissionError):
   621→                            pass
   622→
   623→                    indexes.append(
   624→                        {
   625→                            "name": index_dir.name,
   626→                            "type": "cli",
   627→                            "status": status,
   628→                            "size_mb": size_mb,
   629→                            "path": index_dir,
   630→                        }
   631→                    )
   632→
   633→        # 2. Apps format: *.leann.meta.json files anywhere in the project
   634→        cli_indexes_dir = project_path / ".leann" / "indexes"
   635→        for meta_file in project_path.rglob("*.leann.meta.json"):
   636→            if meta_file.is_file():
   637→                # Skip CLI-built indexes (which store meta under .leann/indexes/<name>/)
   638→                try:
   639→                    if cli_indexes_dir.exists() and cli_indexes_dir in meta_file.parents:
   640→                        continue
   641→                except Exception:
   642→                    pass
   643→                # Skip meta files that live under excluded directories
   644→                try:
   645→                    meta_parent_resolved = meta_file.parent.resolve()
   646→                    if any(
   647→                        meta_parent_resolved.is_relative_to(ex_dir)
   648→                        for ex_dir in exclude_dirs_resolved
   649→                    ):
   650→                        continue
   651→                except Exception:
   652→                    # best effort; if resolve or comparison fails, do not exclude
   653→                    pass
   654→                # Use the parent directory name as the app index display name
   655→                display_name = meta_file.parent.name
   656→                # Extract file base used to store files
   657→                file_base = meta_file.name.replace(".leann.meta.json", "")
   658→
   659→                # Apps indexes are considered complete if the .leann.meta.json file exists
   660→                status = "✅"
   661→
   662→                # Calculate total size of all related files (use file base)
   663→                size_mb = 0
   664→                try:
   665→                    index_dir = meta_file.parent
   666→                    for related_file in index_dir.glob(f"{file_base}.leann*"):
   667→                        size_mb += related_file.stat().st_size / (1024 * 1024)
   668→                except (OSError, PermissionError):
   669→                    pass
   670→
   671→                indexes.append(
   672→                    {
   673→                        "name": display_name,
   674→                        "type": "app",
   675→                        "status": status,
   676→                        "size_mb": size_mb,
   677→                        "path": meta_file,
   678→                    }
   679→                )
   680→
   681→        return indexes

   699→    def _find_all_matching_indexes(self, index_name: str):
   700→        """Find all indexes with the given name across all projects"""
   701→        matches = []
   702→
   703→        # Get all registered projects
   704→        global_registry = Path.home() / ".leann" / "projects.json"
   705→        all_projects = []
   706→
   707→        if global_registry.exists():
   708→            try:
   709→                import json
   710→
   711→                with open(global_registry) as f:
   712→                    all_projects = json.load(f)
   713→            except Exception:
   714→                pass
   715→
   716→        # Always include current project
   717→        current_path = Path.cwd()
   718→        if str(current_path) not in all_projects:
   719→            all_projects.append(str(current_path))
   720→
   721→        # Search across all projects
   722→        for project_dir in all_projects:
   723→            project_path = Path(project_dir)
   724→            if not project_path.exists():
   725→                continue
   726→
   727→            # 1) CLI-format index under .leann/indexes/<name>
   728→            index_dir = project_path / ".leann" / "indexes" / index_name
   729→            if index_dir.exists():
   730→                is_current = project_path == current_path
   731→                matches.append(
   732→                    {
   733→                        "project_path": project_path,
   734→                        "index_dir": index_dir,
   735→                        "is_current": is_current,
   736→                        "kind": "cli",
   737→                    }
   738→                )
   739→
   740→            # 2) App-format indexes
   741→            # We support two ways of addressing apps:
   742→            #   a) by the file base (e.g., `pdf_documents`)
   743→            #   b) by the parent directory name (e.g., `new_txt`)
   744→            seen_app_meta = set()
   745→
   746→            # 2a) by file base
   747→            for meta_file in project_path.rglob(f"{index_name}.leann.meta.json"):
   748→                if meta_file.is_file():
   749→                    # Skip CLI-built indexes' meta under .leann/indexes
   750→                    try:

    38→def compute_embeddings(
    39→    chunks: list[str],
    40→    model_name: str,
    41→    mode: str = "sentence-transformers",
    42→    use_server: bool = True,
    43→    port: Optional[int] = None,
    44→    is_build=False,
    45→    provider_options: Optional[dict[str, Any]] = None,
    46→) -> np.ndarray:
    47→    """
    48→    Computes embeddings using different backends.
    49→
    50→    Args:
    51→        chunks: List of text chunks to embed
    52→        model_name: Name of the embedding model
    53→        mode: Embedding backend mode. Options:
    54→            - "sentence-transformers": Use sentence-transformers library (default)
    55→            - "mlx": Use MLX backend for Apple Silicon
    56→            - "openai": Use OpenAI embedding API
    57→            - "gemini": Use Google Gemini embedding API
    58→        use_server: Whether to use embedding server (True for search, False for build)
    59→
    60→    Returns:
    61→        numpy array of embeddings
    62→    """
    63→    if use_server:
    64→        # Use embedding server (for search/query)
    65→        if port is None:
    66→            raise ValueError("port is required when use_server is True")
    67→        return compute_embeddings_via_server(chunks, model_name, port=port)
    68→    else:
    69→        # Use direct computation (for build_index)
    70→        from .embedding_compute import (
    71→            compute_embeddings as compute_embeddings_direct,
    72→        )
    73→
    74→        return compute_embeddings_direct(
    75→            chunks,
    76→            model_name,
    77→            mode=mode,
    78→            is_build=is_build,
    79→            provider_options=provider_options,
    80→        )

    83→def compute_embeddings_via_server(chunks: list[str], model_name: str, port: int) -> np.ndarray:
    84→    """Computes embeddings using sentence-transformers.
    85→
    86→    Args:
    87→        chunks: List of text chunks to embed
    88→        model_name: Name of the sentence transformer model
    89→    """
    90→    logger.info(
    91→        f"Computing embeddings for {len(chunks)} chunks using SentenceTransformer model '{model_name}' (via embedding server)..."
    92→    )
    93→    import msgpack
    94→    import numpy as np
    95→    import zmq
    96→
    97→    # Connect to embedding server
    98→    context = zmq.Context()
    99→    socket = context.socket(zmq.REQ)
   100→    socket.connect(f"tcp://localhost:{port}")
   101→
   102→    # Send chunks to server for embedding computation
   103→    request = chunks
   104→    socket.send(msgpack.packb(request))
   105→
   106→    # Receive embeddings from server
   107→    response = socket.recv()
   108→    embeddings_list = msgpack.unpackb(response)
   109→
   110→    # Convert back to numpy array
   111→    embeddings = np.array(embeddings_list, dtype=np.float32)
   112→
   113→    socket.close()
   114→    context.term()
   115→
   116→    return embeddings

   127→class PassageManager:
   128→    def __init__(
   129→        self, passage_sources: list[dict[str, Any]], metadata_file_path: Optional[str] = None
   130→    ):
   131→        self.offset_maps: dict[str, dict[str, int]] = {}
   132→        self.passage_files: dict[str, str] = {}
   133→        # Avoid materializing a single gigantic global map to reduce memory
   134→        # footprint on very large corpora (e.g., 60M+ passages). Instead, keep
   135→        # per-shard maps and do a lightweight per-shard lookup on demand.
   136→        self._total_count: int = 0
   137→        self.filter_engine = MetadataFilterEngine()  # Initialize filter engine
   138→
   139→        # Derive index base name for standard sibling fallbacks, e.g., <index_name>.passages.*
   140→        index_name_base = None
   141→        if metadata_file_path:
   142→            meta_name = Path(metadata_file_path).name
   143→            if meta_name.endswith(".meta.json"):
   144→                index_name_base = meta_name[: -len(".meta.json")]
   145→
   146→        for source in passage_sources:
   147→            assert source["type"] == "jsonl", "only jsonl is supported"
   148→            passage_file = source.get("path", "")
   149→            index_file = source.get("index_path", "")  # .idx file
   150→
   151→            # Fix path resolution - relative paths should be relative to metadata file directory
   152→            def _resolve_candidates(
   153→                primary: str,
   154→                relative_key: str,
   155→                default_name: Optional[str],
   156→                source_dict: dict[str, Any],
   157→            ) -> list[Path]:
   158→                """
   159→                Build an ordered list of candidate paths. For relative paths specified in
   160→                metadata, prefer resolution relative to the metadata file directory first,
   161→                then fall back to CWD-based resolution, and finally to conventional
   162→                sibling defaults (e.g., <index_base>.passages.idx / .jsonl).
   163→                """
   164→                candidates: list[Path] = []
   165→                # 1) Primary path
   166→                if primary:
   167→                    p = Path(primary)
   168→                    if p.is_absolute():
   169→                        candidates.append(p)
   170→                    else:
   171→                        # Prefer metadata-relative resolution for relative paths
   172→                        if metadata_file_path:
   173→                            candidates.append(Path(metadata_file_path).parent / p)
   174→                        # Also consider CWD-relative as a fallback for legacy layouts
   175→                        candidates.append(Path.cwd() / p)
   176→                # 2) metadata-relative explicit relative key (if present)
   177→                if metadata_file_path and source_dict.get(relative_key):
   178→                    candidates.append(Path(metadata_file_path).parent / source_dict[relative_key])
   179→                # 3) metadata-relative standard sibling filename
   180→                if metadata_file_path and default_name:
   181→                    candidates.append(Path(metadata_file_path).parent / default_name)
   182→                return candidates
   183→
   184→            # Build candidate lists and pick first existing; otherwise keep last candidate for error message
   185→            idx_default = f"{index_name_base}.passages.idx" if index_name_base else None
   186→            idx_candidates = _resolve_candidates(
   187→                index_file, "index_path_relative", idx_default, source
   188→            )
   189→            pas_default = f"{index_name_base}.passages.jsonl" if index_name_base else None
   190→            pas_candidates = _resolve_candidates(passage_file, "path_relative", pas_default, source)
   191→
   192→            def _pick_existing(cands: list[Path]) -> str:
   193→                for c in cands:
   194→                    if c.exists():
   195→                        return str(c.resolve())
   196→                # Fallback to last candidate (best guess) even if not exists; will error below
   197→                return str(cands[-1].resolve()) if cands else ""
   198→
   199→            index_file = _pick_existing(idx_candidates)
   200→            passage_file = _pick_existing(pas_candidates)
   201→
   202→            if not Path(index_file).exists():
   203→                raise FileNotFoundError(f"Passage index file not found: {index_file}")
   204→
   205→            with open(index_file, "rb") as f:
   206→                offset_map: dict[str, int] = pickle.load(f)
   207→                self.offset_maps[passage_file] = offset_map
   208→                self.passage_files[passage_file] = passage_file
   209→                self._total_count += len(offset_map)
   210→
   211→    def get_passage(self, passage_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
   212→        # Fast path: check each shard map (there are typically few shards).
   213→        # This avoids building a massive combined dict while keeping lookups
   214→        # bounded by the number of shards.
   215→        for passage_file, offset_map in self.offset_maps.items():
   216→            try:
   217→                offset = offset_map[passage_id]
   218→                with open(passage_file, encoding="utf-8") as f:
   219→                    f.seek(offset)
   220→                    return json.loads(f.readline())
   221→            except KeyError:
   222→                continue
   223→        raise KeyError(f"Passage ID not found: {passage_id}")

   225→    def filter_search_results(
   226→        self,
   227→        search_results: list[SearchResult],
   228→        metadata_filters: Optional[dict[str, dict[str, Union[str, int, float, bool, list]]]],
   229→    ) -> list[SearchResult]:
   230→        """
   231→        Apply metadata filters to search results.
   232→
   233→        Args:
   234→            search_results: List of SearchResult objects
   235→            metadata_filters: Filter specifications to apply
   236→
   237→        Returns:
   238→            Filtered list of SearchResult objects
   239→        """
   240→        if not metadata_filters:
   241→            return search_results
   242→
   243→        logger.debug(f"Applying metadata filters to {len(search_results)} results")
   244→
   245→        # Convert SearchResult objects to dictionaries for the filter engine
   246→        result_dicts = []
   247→        for result in search_results:
   248→            result_dicts.append(
   249→                {
   250→                    "id": result.id,
   251→                    "score": result.score,
   252→                    "text": result.text,
   253→                    "metadata": result.metadata,
   254→                }
   255→            )
   256→
   257→        # Apply filters using the filter engine
   258→        filtered_dicts = self.filter_engine.apply_filters(result_dicts, metadata_filters)
   259→
   260→        # Convert back to SearchResult objects
   261→        filtered_results = []
   262→        for result_dict in filtered_dicts:
   263→            filtered_results.append(
   264→                SearchResult(
   265→                    id=result_dict["id"],
   266→                    score=result_dict["score"],
   267→                    text=result_dict["text"],
   268→                    metadata=result_dict["metadata"],
   269→                )
   270→            )
   271→
   272→        logger.debug(f"Filtered results: {len(filtered_results)} remaining")
   273→        return filtered_results
   274→
   275→    def __len__(self) -> int:
   276→        return self._total_count

   279→class LeannBuilder:
   280→    def __init__(
   281→        self,
   282→        backend_name: str,
   283→        embedding_model: str = "facebook/contriever",
   284→        dimensions: Optional[int] = None,
   285→        embedding_mode: str = "sentence-transformers",
   286→        embedding_options: Optional[dict[str, Any]] = None,
   287→        **backend_kwargs,
   288→    ):
   289→        self.backend_name = backend_name
   290→        # Normalize incompatible combinations early (for consistent metadata)
   291→        if backend_name == "hnsw":
   292→            is_recompute = backend_kwargs.get("is_recompute", True)
   293→            is_compact = backend_kwargs.get("is_compact", True)
   294→            if is_recompute is False and is_compact is True:
   295→                warnings.warn(
   296→                    "HNSW with is_recompute=False requires non-compact storage. Forcing is_compact=False.",
   297→                    UserWarning,
   298→                    stacklevel=2,
   299→                )
   300→                backend_kwargs["is_compact"] = False
   301→
   302→        backend_factory: Optional[LeannBackendFactoryInterface] = BACKEND_REGISTRY.get(backend_name)
   303→        if backend_factory is None:
   304→            raise ValueError(f"Backend '{backend_name}' not found or not registered.")
   305→        self.backend_factory = backend_factory
   306→        self.embedding_model = embedding_model
   307→        self.dimensions = dimensions
   308→        self.embedding_mode = embedding_mode
   309→        self.embedding_options = embedding_options or {}
   310→
   311→        # Check if we need to use cosine distance for normalized embeddings
   312→        normalized_embeddings_models = {
   313→            # OpenAI models
   314→            ("openai", "text-embedding-ada-002"),
   315→            ("openai", "text-embedding-3-small"),
   316→            ("openai", "text-embedding-3-large"),
   317→            # Voyage AI models
   318→            ("voyage", "voyage-2"),
   319→            ("voyage", "voyage-3"),
   320→            ("voyage", "voyage-large-2"),
   321→            ("voyage", "voyage-multilingual-2"),
   322→            ("voyage", "voyage-code-2"),
   323→            # Cohere models
   324→            ("cohere", "embed-english-v3.0"),
   325→            ("cohere", "embed-multilingual-v3.0"),
   326→            ("cohere", "embed-english-light-v3.0"),
   327→            ("cohere", "embed-multilingual-light-v3.0"),
   328→        }
   329→
   330→        # Also check for patterns in model names
   331→        is_normalized = False
   332→        current_model_lower = embedding_model.lower()
   333→        current_mode_lower = embedding_mode.lower()
   334→
   335→        # Check exact matches
   336→        for mode, model in normalized_embeddings_models:
   337→            if (current_mode_lower == mode and current_model_lower == model) or (
   338→                mode in current_mode_lower and model in current_model_lower
   339→            ):
   340→                is_normalized = True
   341→                break
   342→
   343→        # Check patterns
   344→        if not is_normalized:
   345→            # OpenAI patterns
   346→            if "openai" in current_mode_lower or "openai" in current_model_lower:
   347→                if any(
   348→                    pattern in current_model_lower
   349→                    for pattern in ["text-embedding", "ada", "3-small", "3-large"]
   350→                ):
   351→                    is_normalized = True
   352→            # Voyage patterns
   353→            elif "voyage" in current_mode_lower or "voyage" in current_model_lower:
   354→                is_normalized = True
   355→            # Cohere patterns
   356→            elif "cohere" in current_mode_lower or "cohere" in current_model_lower:
   357→                if "embed" in current_model_lower:
   358→                    is_normalized = True
   359→
   360→        # Handle distance metric
   361→        if is_normalized and "distance_metric" not in backend_kwargs:
   362→            backend_kwargs["distance_metric"] = "cosine"
   363→            warnings.warn(
   364→                f"Detected normalized embeddings model '{embedding_model}' with mode '{embedding_mode}'. "
   365→                f"Automatically setting distance_metric='cosine' for optimal performance. "
   366→                f"Normalized embeddings (L2 norm = 1) should use cosine similarity instead of MIPS.",
   367→                UserWarning,
   368→                stacklevel=2,
   369→            )
   370→        elif is_normalized and backend_kwargs.get("distance_metric", "").lower() != "cosine":
   371→            current_metric = backend_kwargs.get("distance_metric", "mips")
   372→            warnings.warn(
   373→                f"Warning: Using '{current_metric}' distance metric with normalized embeddings model "
   374→                f"'{embedding_model}' may lead to suboptimal search results. "
   375→                f"Consider using 'cosine' distance metric for better performance.",
   376→                UserWarning,
   377→                stacklevel=2,
   378→            )
   379→
   380→        self.backend_kwargs = backend_kwargs
   381→        self.chunks: list[dict[str, Any]] = []

   383→    def add_text(self, text: str, metadata: Optional[dict[str, Any]] = None):
   384→        if metadata is None:
   385→            metadata = {}
   386→        passage_id = metadata.get("id", str(len(self.chunks)))
   387→        chunk_data = {"id": passage_id, "text": text, "metadata": metadata}

   390→    def build_index(self, index_path: str):
   391→        if not self.chunks:
   392→            raise ValueError("No chunks added.")
   393→
   394→        # Filter out invalid/empty text chunks early to keep passage and embedding counts aligned
   395→        valid_chunks: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
   396→        skipped = 0
   397→        for chunk in self.chunks:
   398→            text = chunk.get("text", "")
   399→            if isinstance(text, str) and text.strip():
   400→                valid_chunks.append(chunk)
   401→            else:
   402→                skipped += 1
   403→        if skipped > 0:
   404→            print(
   405→                f"Warning: Skipping {skipped} empty/invalid text chunk(s). Processing {len(valid_chunks)} valid chunks"
   406→            )
   407→            self.chunks = valid_chunks
   408→            if not self.chunks:
   409→                raise ValueError("All provided chunks are empty or invalid. Nothing to index.")
   410→        if self.dimensions is None:
   411→            self.dimensions = len(
   412→                compute_embeddings(
   413→                    ["dummy"],
   414→                    self.embedding_model,
   415→                    self.embedding_mode,
   416→                    use_server=False,
   417→                    provider_options=self.embedding_options,
   418→                )[0]
   419→            )
   420→        path = Path(index_path)
   421→        index_dir = path.parent
   422→        index_name = path.name
   423→        index_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   424→        passages_file = index_dir / f"{index_name}.passages.jsonl"
   425→        offset_file = index_dir / f"{index_name}.passages.idx"
   426→        offset_map = {}
   427→        with open(passages_file, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
   428→            try:
   429→                from tqdm import tqdm
   430→
   431→                chunk_iterator = tqdm(self.chunks, desc="Writing passages", unit="chunk")
   432→            except ImportError:
   433→                chunk_iterator = self.chunks
   434→
   435→            for chunk in chunk_iterator:
   436→                offset = f.tell()
   437→                json.dump(
   438→                    {
   439→                        "id": chunk["id"],
   440→                        "text": chunk["text"],
   441→                        "metadata": chunk["metadata"],
   442→                    },
   443→                    f,
   444→                    ensure_ascii=False,
   445→                )
   446→                f.write("\n")
   447→                offset_map[chunk["id"]] = offset
   448→        with open(offset_file, "wb") as f:
   449→            pickle.dump(offset_map, f)
   450→        texts_to_embed = [c["text"] for c in self.chunks]
   451→        embeddings = compute_embeddings(
   452→            texts_to_embed,
   453→            self.embedding_model,
   454→            self.embedding_mode,
   455→            use_server=False,
   456→            is_build=True,
   457→            provider_options=self.embedding_options,
   458→        )
   459→        string_ids = [chunk["id"] for chunk in self.chunks]
   460→        # Persist ID map alongside index so backends that return integer labels can remap to passage IDs
   461→        try:
   462→            idmap_file = (
   463→                index_dir
   464→                / f"{index_name[: -len('.leann')] if index_name.endswith('.leann') else index_name}.ids.txt"
   465→            )
   466→            with open(idmap_file, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
   467→                for sid in string_ids:
   468→                    f.write(str(sid) + "\n")
   469→        except Exception:
   470→            pass
   471→        current_backend_kwargs = {**self.backend_kwargs, "dimensions": self.dimensions}
   472→        builder_instance = self.backend_factory.builder(**current_backend_kwargs)
   473→        builder_instance.build(embeddings, string_ids, index_path, **current_backend_kwargs)
   474→        leann_meta_path = index_dir / f"{index_name}.meta.json"
   475→        meta_data = {
   476→            "version": "1.0",
   477→            "backend_name": self.backend_name,
   478→            "embedding_model": self.embedding_model,
   479→            "dimensions": self.dimensions,
   480→            "backend_kwargs": self.backend_kwargs,
   481→            "embedding_mode": self.embedding_mode,
   482→            "passage_sources": [
   483→                {
   484→                    "type": "jsonl",
   485→                    # Preserve existing relative file names (backward-compatible)
   486→                    "path": passages_file.name,
   487→                    "index_path": offset_file.name,
   488→                    # Add optional redundant relative keys for remote build portability (non-breaking)
   489→                    "path_relative": passages_file.name,
   490→                    "index_path_relative": offset_file.name,
   491→                }
   492→            ],
   493→        }
   494→
   495→        if self.embedding_options:
   496→            meta_data["embedding_options"] = self.embedding_options
   497→
   498→        # Add storage status flags for HNSW backend
   499→        if self.backend_name == "hnsw":
   500→            is_compact = self.backend_kwargs.get("is_compact", True)
   501→            is_recompute = self.backend_kwargs.get("is_recompute", True)
   502→            meta_data["is_compact"] = is_compact
   503→            meta_data["is_pruned"] = bool(is_recompute)
   504→        with open(leann_meta_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
   505→            json.dump(meta_data, f, indent=2)

   507→    def build_index_from_embeddings(self, index_path: str, embeddings_file: str):
   508→        """
   509→        Build an index from pre-computed embeddings stored in a pickle file.
   510→
   511→        Args:
   512→            index_path: Path where the index will be saved
   513→            embeddings_file: Path to pickle file containing (ids, embeddings) tuple
   514→        """
   515→        # Load pre-computed embeddings
   516→        with open(embeddings_file, "rb") as f:
   517→            data = pickle.load(f)
   518→
   519→        if not isinstance(data, tuple) or len(data) != 2:
   520→            raise ValueError(
   521→                f"Invalid embeddings file format. Expected tuple with 2 elements, got {type(data)}"
   522→            )
   523→
   524→        ids, embeddings = data
   525→
   526→        if not isinstance(embeddings, np.ndarray):
   527→            raise ValueError(f"Expected embeddings to be numpy array, got {type(embeddings)}")
   528→
   529→        if len(ids) != embeddings.shape[0]:
   530→            raise ValueError(
   531→                f"Mismatch between number of IDs ({len(ids)}) and embeddings ({embeddings.shape[0]})"
   532→            )
   533→
   534→        # Validate/set dimensions
   535→        embedding_dim = embeddings.shape[1]
   536→        if self.dimensions is None:
   537→            self.dimensions = embedding_dim
   538→        elif self.dimensions != embedding_dim:
   539→            raise ValueError(f"Dimension mismatch: expected {self.dimensions}, got {embedding_dim}")
   540→
   541→        logger.info(
   542→            f"Building index from precomputed embeddings: {len(ids)} items, {embedding_dim} dimensions"
   543→        )
   544→
   545→        # Ensure we have text data for each embedding
   546→        if len(self.chunks) != len(ids):
   547→            # If no text chunks provided, create placeholder text entries
   548→            if not self.chunks:
   549→                logger.info("No text chunks provided, creating placeholder entries...")
   550→                for id_val in ids:
   551→                    self.add_text(
   552→                        f"Document {id_val}",
   553→                        metadata={"id": str(id_val), "from_embeddings": True},
   554→                    )
   555→            else:
   556→                raise ValueError(
   557→                    f"Number of text chunks ({len(self.chunks)}) doesn't match number of embeddings ({len(ids)})"
   558→                )
   559→
   560→        # Build file structure
   561→        path = Path(index_path)
   562→        index_dir = path.parent
   563→        index_name = path.name
   564→        index_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   565→        passages_file = index_dir / f"{index_name}.passages.jsonl"
   566→        offset_file = index_dir / f"{index_name}.passages.idx"
   567→
   568→        # Write passages and create offset map
   569→        offset_map = {}
   570→        with open(passages_file, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
   571→            for chunk in self.chunks:
   572→                offset = f.tell()
   573→                json.dump(
   574→                    {
   575→                        "id": chunk["id"],
   576→                        "text": chunk["text"],
   577→                        "metadata": chunk["metadata"],
   578→                    },
   579→                    f,
   580→                    ensure_ascii=False,
   581→                )
   582→                f.write("\n")

   644→    def update_index(self, index_path: str):

   660→            raise FileNotFoundError("Index metadata or passage files are missing; cannot update.")
   661→        if not index_file.exists():
   662→            raise FileNotFoundError(f"HNSW index file not found: {index_file}")
   663→

   665→            meta = json.load(f)
   666→        backend_name = meta.get("backend_name")
   667→        if backend_name != self.backend_name:
   668→            raise ValueError(

   670→            )
